seal.statement: The live-surface guards exempt exactly one file per quest, its canonical append-only log, and that exemption rests on an enforced invariant rather than a comment: a checker refuses any in-place rewrite or deletion of a committed quest log, admits appends and new logs, and runs in the static gate, while the exemption boundary itself (a quest's authored record, its evidence, deleted v1 directories, and live steering, scripts and docs that merely name the same strings) is asserted adversarially by tests.

text: Publication-gate finding against the landed head 5271defb5, not a defect in the landing: npm run publish refused at the static-analysis stage because audit:no-kiro reported 9 disallowed references inside migrated quest logs. Its whitelist exempted solve/log/, solve/report/ and solve/autonomous/, three directories the cutover deleted; the immutable records they protected now live at solve/quests/<id>/log.ndjson. scripts/check-no-legacy-naming.js carried the same three stale prefixes, latent because nothing currently trips it. Chronology: landed 5271defb5, publish refused, this finding, owner repair, new candidate head, publish.

The exemption's premise was unenforced, demonstrated twice and restored both times byte-identically to the landed commit: flipping a recorded verifier verdict from approve to reject inside solve/quests/solve-v2-phase-2/log.ndjson was noticed by nothing. Not audit:no-kiro, not the binary guard, not legacy-corpus-drift (that log is not migration corpus, and for migrated logs only the pre-migration prefix is covered), not the quest state. So the guards were exempting a channel that could be written, which is exactly what a historical-record exemption must not be. That is why this is a sealed quest rather than a direct fix.

Both live-surface guards now ask scripts/solve/store.js whether a path is a quest log (new isQuestLogPath: exactly solve/quests/<canonical-id>/log.ndjson, id validated against the schema), so neither restates quest layout. The exemption is narrower than the v1 one it replaces: a quest's authored record and its evidence stay governed, and the evidence exemption I first wrote was removed once the guard proved clean without it, leaving evidence classification to the evidence owner. The three prefixes naming deleted v1 directories are gone from both guards rather than left as stale taxonomy. New scripts/checks/check-quest-log-append-only.js refuses any in-place rewrite, truncation or deletion of a committed quest log and is wired into test:static as audit:quest-log-append-only, so the immutability the exemption rests on is enforced. Adversarial boundary tests cover the canonical log, the sibling record, evidence, non-canonical ids, lookalike paths, the deleted v1 prefixes and live steering/scripts/docs that name the same strings.

Hardened the invariant against the case a snapshot comparison cannot see. The first checker compared one tree against one base, which protects nothing once a rewrite is itself committed, and cannot protect a log that first appeared after the publication base at all: from that base every one of the 826 canonical logs created in 5271defb5 looks new. The checker now reasons over commit transitions: for each parent to child edge in the admitted range, every changed canonical quest log must carry its parent's bytes as an exact prefix, with the working tree checked as the final edge so a rewrite is also refused before commit. Creation has no parent bytes and passes, deletion cannot satisfy the prefix, and a rename is a deletion of the committed path (diff runs with --no-renames so it is reported as one). The range comes from the change-selection owner (resolvedCheckBase) falling back to the merge base with origin/main, so this check holds no branch-topology policy and the store holds no git-range policy. Three concerns stay separate: the store classifies a path, this audit owns the mutation invariant, and each guard owns its own policy. Runs in 0.3s over the real stacked state.

Falsifiers now proven in temporary repositories with real commit sequences: a new canonical log may be introduced; a later commit may append; a same-length byte change before the previous EOF is refused at that transition; truncation is refused; deletion is refused; a rename is refused as deletion of the committed path; a log introduced after the base and rewritten in a later commit of the same unpublished stack is refused even though the working tree then matches HEAD (the test asserts a base-at-newest-commit comparison would have passed it, which is what makes the transition check necessary); several append commits in one stack are admitted; and quest.json, evidence, lookalikes and non-canonical ids stay outside the boundary.

Two facts checked before landing rather than assumed. (1) Merges: scripts/publish-head.js requires only that origin/main is an ancestor of HEAD (merge-base --is-ancestor); nothing forbids a merge commit inside the admitted range, and the current range happens to be linear. So the checker compares a commit against every parent, not the first: two branches appending to the same log diverge, no merge can preserve both prefixes, and dropping one side's entries is the history loss this refuses. A falsifier drives a real merge that keeps one side and asserts refusal. No topology policy is duplicated; the range still comes from the change-selection owner. (2) A byte-offset defect found by running against the real repository, not the fixtures: rewriting the batch-stream scan as a string search made character and byte offsets diverge on any log holding non-ASCII content, mis-slicing every later blob and reporting hundreds of clean logs as truncated. ASCII fixtures could not see it; a multi-byte falsifier now covers it.
